title: Fresnel Rim in a Material Snippet
prompt: Add a fresnel rim light term to a surface shader
explanation: The fresnel falloff 1 - dot(N, V) is near zero facing the camera and approaches one at the silhouette; raising it to a power tightens the rim. Adding the result to Cf gives a cheap, art-directable edge light entirely in VEX.

title: World-Space Noise Tint
prompt: Blend two colours with low-frequency world-space noise
explanation: Sampling noise at the shading position P gives a smooth 0-1 field that lerp() uses to mix two colours. Using world-space P keeps the pattern anchored to the object even under animation.

title: Vertical Gradient Blend
prompt: Blend two colours by height for a simple gradient material
explanation: fit() remaps world height into 0-1 between the chosen bounds and clamp() keeps it in range past the limits. The result drives a vertical colour blend -- a building block for stratified rock, gradient backdrops and sky-style tints.

title: Procedural Noise Displacement
prompt: Displace a surface along its normal in a displacement shader
explanation: Centring the noise around zero (-0.5..0.5, scaled) gives a signed displacement so the surface pushes both in and out. Moving P along the normal is true geometric displacement; remember to recompute N or the shading will still reflect the original surface.

houdini_version_notes: Compile with vcc and bind as a material, or paste into an Inline VOP.
title: Standalone CVEX Surface Shader
prompt: Write a minimal standalone CVEX surface shader with a lambert term
explanation: A cvex function declares its bound parameters in the signature; 'export' marks outputs the shading network reads back (here Cf). The body is an ambient-plus-lambert term against a fixed light direction -- the smallest complete shader you can compile with vcc.

title: Procedural UV Checker
prompt: Generate a checkerboard pattern from UV coordinates in a shader
explanation: Flooring the scaled UVs gives integer tile indices; the parity of their sum alternates 0/1 across the grid, producing a checker. It is the canonical UV-debug pattern and a base for tiled procedural textures.
